full_description: Job Application for Data Scientist, Project Success and Innovation at American Institutes for Research Back to jobs New Data Scientist, Project Success and Innovation US-Remote | US-VA-Arlington | US-NC-Chapel Hill | US-IL-Chicago | US-CA-Sacramento | US-TX-Austin Apply AIR is seeking a Data Scientist to join the Project Success and Innovation (PSI) team and the Employment and Economic Opportunity Program (EEOP ), providing advanced technical expertise to support innovation development, scaling efforts, and applied research and analytics across project teams. Within PSI, the Data Scientist will contribute to AIR’s Innovation Lab by co-designing, developing, and scaling solutions that strengthen and amplify effective practices across diverse technical and operational workflows. Within EEOP, the Data Scientist will lead end-to-end quantitative workflows, including establishing and maintaining reproducible analytic environments, managing and quality assuring complex datasets, reviewing and strengthening junior staff members’ code, and conducting advanced statistical analyses. These analyses may include causal approaches, such as experimental and quasi-experimental designs, as well as non-causal approaches, including descriptive, predictive, and explanatory modeling. The Data Scientist will also help expand AIR’s capacity to responsibly apply machine learning methods in support of both research and operational objectives, while translating technical findings into clear, actionable products for clients, partners, and other stakeholders. Candidates hired for the position may work remotely within the United States (U.S.) or from one of our U.S. office locations. This does not include U.S. territories. About AIR: Founded in 1946 and headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, the American Institutes for Research (AIR) is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization that conducts behavioral and social science research and delivers technical assistance to address some of the most pressing challenges in the United States and globally. We generate evidence and apply data-driven solutions that expand opportunities and improve lives for all. Responsibilities The responsibilities for the position include: PSI (approximately 50 %) Build and maintain shared analytic tools, including code libraries, project templates, and pipelines, that research teams across AIR can adopt and reuse. Write documentation, training materials, and onboarding guides that make modern tooling accessible to staff with varying levels of technical experience. Support project teams adopting new tools and workflows by answering questions, troubleshooting, and relaying recurring problems back to the team. Prototype and test new tools and platforms, including machine learning and AI applications such as large language models, and help assess their fit and responsible use at AIR. Help maintain deployed tools by triaging issues, fixing bugs, and tracking user feedback. Contribute to work plans, timelines, and progress tracking for PSI activities, communicating regularly with PSI leadership. EEOP (approximately 50 %) Conduct quantitative analyses on research and evaluation projects, including analyses for causal and non-causal research questions. Serve as lead analyst on discrete studies or analytic components, with support from senior researchers. Manage, clean, and quality-assure complex datasets from multiple sources. Build and document reproducible analytic workflows and quality control procedures. Review analytic code produced by research associates and other junior staff, and support their development in reproducible analysis and documentation practices. Contribute to study design and analytic planning discussions. Draft analytic sections of client reports, technical memos, and presentations, and help translate findings for non-technical audiences. Track deliverables and timelines for assigned analytic tasks. Contribute technical content to proposals. Qualifications: Education, Knowledge, and Experience Master's or doctoral degree in a quantitative field, including statistics, computational social science, education data science, statistics, economics, quantitative psychology, quantitative methods, data science, or a related discipline, recently completed or nearing completion. Coursework or applied experience in causal inference and statistical modeling. Experience with complex survey data, sampling, and large-scale administrative, longitudinal, or linked datasets. Experience applying quantitative methods to education, health, or social policy questions. Experience or familiarity with machine learning and AI methods, including applications of large language models in research. Interest in building tools that other people use, and willingness to support them in doing so. Familiarity with data common in applied social research, such as administrative records, longitudinal student or program data, survey data, or text. Experience with restricted-use or confidential data. Prior work building or maintaining code used by others. Skills Proficiency in R and/or Python. Working knowledge of Stata. Familiarity with version control (Git and Github) and an interest in reproducible research practices. Familiarity with literate programming and reproducible reporting tools such as Quarto, R Markdown, or Jupyter. Ability to communicate effectively with colleagues who have varying levels of technical experience. Ability to write clearly about technical work for non-technical readers. Disclosures: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the U.S. on a full-time basis. Employment-based visa sponsorship (including H-1B sponsorship) is not available for this position. Depending on project work, qualified candidates may need to meet certain residency requirements. American Institutes for Research is an equal employment opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without discrimination on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law, including, but not limited to, actual or perceived race (including traits historically associated with race, such as hair texture, hair type, and protective hairstyles such as braid, locs, and twists), creed, color, religion, alienage or national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition (e.g., cancer), sex, gender, gender identity or expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, civil union status, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, genetic information, or military or veteran status. AIR adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. All selected candidates will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles and will therefore undergo reference and background checks. AIR maintains a drug-free work environment. ACCESSIBILITY NOTICE: If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process due to a physical or mental disability, please send an email to Taliba Boone at tboone@air.org or call 202.403.5000. Description Are you passionate about translating scientific research into real-world impact at massive scale? PXT Central Science (PXTCS) builds the analytical foundations that shape how Amazon attracts, develops, and retains talent at a scale no other company operates. Our models and research directly influence decisions affecting over a million employees worldwide, from compensation and attrition strategy to employee engagement and workforce planning The L5 Research Scientist in Survey Science contributes to the science behind Amazon's state-of-the-art employee surveys, setting the standard for how Amazon measures what its employees are experiencing. The questions that matter most in this role are the ones numbers alone cannot settle, and that often run ahead of demand — identifying the challenges leaders will face before they ask, and building the methods to address them. How is the culture changing as the company evolves? What are employees experiencing that no metric on a dashboard captures? Where are employee concerns emerging that have not yet shown up in any data? These factors drive business outcomes, resist clean quantification, and require creative measurement approaches to address. Key job responsibilities - Design, develop, and evaluate mathematical, statistical, and machine learning models to address complex business problems, ensuring solutions are scalable, reliable, and performant in production environments. - Apply a breadth of scientific techniques — including generative AI approaches where appropriate — to frame ambiguous business challenges into well-defined research problems, working backwards from customer needs to identify the right methodology. - Collaborate with software development engineers and cross-functional partners to translate research prototypes into engineering specifications and production-ready systems, balancing scientific rigor with practical constraints. - Provide guidance on survey methods to teams across PXT, so employee research across Amazon meets a consistent standard. - Develop and audit metrics to quantify solution impact, measure project progress, and gate rollouts based on quality, while identifying opportunities for continuous model improvement. - Mentor other scientists and contribute to the broader scientific community through peer reviews, publications at internal or external venues, and active participation in hiring and team planning. A day in the life You might start your morning reviewing experimental results from a model you deployed last week, then shift into a design discussion with engineering partners about integrating a new approach into an existing system. After lunch, you could be deep in data analysis, exploring patterns that inform your next hypothesis. You'll regularly present findings to teammates, provide scientific reviews for peers across the organization, and carve out time to stay current with the latest research in your field. About the team PXT Central Science is Amazon's people-science R&D organization. We develop causal inference methods, predictive models, and decision-support tools that operate at the intersection of economics, machine learning, and organizational science. Our work spans employee experience, workforce planning, compensation, talent acquisition, and employee relations — always grounded in rigorous methodology and always aimed at real-world impact. Description Amazon Advertising is one of Amazon's fastest growing and most profitable businesses, responsible for defining and delivering a collection of advertising products that drive discovery and sales. Our products and solutions are strategically important to enable our Retail and Marketplace businesses to drive long-term growth. We deliver billions of ad impressions and millions of clicks and break fresh ground in product and technical innovations every day! Demand Tech Experience (DTx), as an org, owns the Amazon Ads Console — the advertiser-facing workspace for creating and managing campaigns, reviewing performance, and acting on recommendations used by millions of advertisers. Our team, DTx Science, is the centralized science team within DTx, dedicated to improving and protecting the advertiser experience across ad consoles through applied science methodologies. The team drives impact through four core functions: Ad Console Personalization, Recommendation Development, Ad Console Experimentation, and DVA Agent Evaluation and Impact Measurement. We leverage a breadth of state-of-the-art techniques such as deep learning, reinforcement learning, LLMs, long term causal modeling as well as sophisticated A/B testing to develop personalized experiences with directly quantifiable business and advertiser success outcomes. We are looking for an accomplished machine learning expert to lead the Applied Science strategy for our recommendation creation and personalization program. In this role, you will work closely with business leaders, stakeholders and cross-functional teams to drive program success through ML-driven solutions. You will shape the applied science roadmap, promote a culture of data-driven decision-making, and deliver significant business impact for millions of advertisers worldwide and the company using advanced data techniques and applied science methodologies. Key job responsibilities As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will - Serve as the technical leader in Machine Learning, driving collaboration between scientists and engineers, guiding efforts within the team and collaborating with other teams. - Conduct hands-on analysis and modeling of large-scale data to generate insights that boost ads revenue while maintaining a positive advertiser and shopper experience. - Lead end-to-end Machine Learning projects that involve high levels of ambiguity, scale, and complexity. - Build, experiment, optimize, and deploy machine learning models, collaborating with software engineers to bring your models into production. - Run A/B experiments, gather data, and perform statistical analysis to validate your models. - Develop scalable and automated processes for large-scale data analysis, model development, validation, and serving. - Explore and research innovative machine learning approaches to push the boundaries of what’s possible. About the team The DTx Science team is the centralized science team within Demand Tech Experience (DTx), dedicated to improving and protecting the advertiser experience across ad consoles through applied science methodologies. The team drives impact through four core functions: Ad Console Personalization, Recommendation Development, Ad Console Experimentation, and DVA Agent Evaluation and Impact Measurement. Improve advertiser experience: Ad Console Personalization and Recommendation Development aim to improve the advertiser ad console experience by providing customized and personalized console experiences for each user and increasing their ad performance with relevant, science-backed onboarding and oppertunty recommendations. Protect advertiser experience: Ad Console Experimentation and DVA Agent Evaluation and Impact Measurement protect the advertiser experience by supporting the organization in making data-driven decisions to launch UX and agentic features that benefit advertisers. Description Are you passionate about using data and machine learning to improve how Amazon reaches customers? The Customer Targeting team is looking for an Applied Scientist to build the science behind the targeting of Amazon's marketing initiatives across channels and ad formats. You will turn business questions into modeling problems and take your solutions from prototype to production, working closely with senior scientists, engineers, and business partners. We are moving targeting toward outcome-based optimization and an AI-native, agentic way of working. In this role you will work on online optimization and reinforcement learning, incrementality modeling, and the next generation of our segment-based targeting model. You will also help build agentic workflows that make targeting decisions transparent and bring science recommendations to the people using them. The right candidate has strong quantitative and statistical skills, hands-on experience with modern ML methods, and is comfortable working through ambiguity in a fast-paced environment. You pay close attention to detail, learn quickly, and work well in a highly collaborative team. Key job responsibilities - Build online optimization (e.g., TSO, bandits) and reinforcement learning methods that optimize targeting decisions for business outcomes rather than proxy metrics. - Develop incrementality and uplift models that estimate the causal impact of targeting, and use them to improve who we target and how much we spend. - Improve the existing segment-based targeting model: engineer and evaluate new features, migrate it to new model architectures, and build automated feedback loops that retrain and improve the model from observed outcomes. - Contribute to the intelligence layer of our agentic system: build components that explain targeting decisions and propose science-driven solutions to business partners. - Design and analyze experiments (A/B tests, causal inference methods) to measure the incremental impact of targeting changes. - Write production-quality model code and partner with engineers to deploy, monitor, and maintain models. - Present methods and results clearly, backed by data, with actionable recommendations for science and business stakeholders. About the team Predictive Targeting builds the systems that decide who sees Amazon's marketing content, and how often, across Amazon's stores and channels. We are engineers and scientists working on one shared problem: making sure customers see the most relevant and engaging marketing, and making each campaign better than the last. Basic Qualifications - 3+ years of building models for business application experience - Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals - Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language - Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing - PhD, or Master's degree and 3+ years of applied research experience Preferred Qualifications - Experience using Unix/Linux - Experience in professional software development - Experience creating processes and improving tools that have measurably improved productivity, quality, or advertiser experience - PhD in a quantitative field such as statistics, mathematics, data science, business analytics, economics, finance, engineering, or computer science, or experience in defining and creating benchmarks for assessing GenAI model performance - Experience with reinforcement learning or online optimization in production, such as multi-armed or contextual bandits, exploration vs. exploitation strategies, or real-time pacing and allocation under budget and frequency constraints. Description Amazon Ads runs one of the largest real-time decision systems in the world. To meet advertiser goals, we process >4 million ad requests per second, and this team decides which of them are worth the compute. We mine a petabyte-scale stream of traffic to tell in-demand, valuable requests apart from wasteful ones, filtering out the noise and forwarding only what brings value to advertisers, all within milli-seconds. Our solutions save millions in compute costs and drive long-term growth for Amazon's Retail and Marketplace businesses. Why you'll love this role: The scientific challenge here is scale and signal: large-scale ML on enormous, high-velocity data, optimization and auction dynamics, and causal measurement of what actually moves the business. Generative AI and LLMs are tools you reach for when they help, not the point of the work. The impact also reaches beyond Amazon: we donated the Dynamic Traffic Engine (DTE) to the IAB Tech Lab as an open-source framework that lets demand-side platforms signal which bid requests they value, so supply-side platforms send fewer wasteful ones and QPS waste drops across the whole programmatic supply chain. We are a highly motivated, collaborative team with an entrepreneurial spirit and a broad mandate to experiment and innovate. You will work alongside talented engineers, product managers, and scientists in a culture that rewards bias for action, innovation, and experimentation. What makes this role unique is the combination of scientific rigor with real-world impact at a scale very few systems reach. Your impact and career growth: Amazon Ads is investing heavily in AI and ML, creating room for scientists to innovate and make their mark. As an Applied Scientist, you will own the science for well-defined supply-optimization problems and take your work end to end, from framing the approach through experimentation and into production with measured business impact. You will partner closely with engineers to productionize your models and with product managers to tie your science to customer and advertiser outcomes. You will share your findings, begin to mentor teammates, and grow your influence on the team's technical direction over time. This is your opportunity to do high-rigor applied science in one of the fastest-growing businesses at Amazon. Learn more about Amazon Ads: https://advertising.amazon.com/ Key job responsibilities As an Applied Scientist in Amazon Ads, you will: - Conduct hands-on data analysis and build large-scale ML models and pipelines for supply optimization. - Take your models end to end, from proof of concept through experimentation, optimization, and deployment into production, working closely with software engineers to productionize them and with product managers and fellow scientists along the way. - Design and run A/B experiments and causal analysis to validate hypotheses, draw insights from petabyte-scale data, and measure real business impact. - Research and apply advanced ML, including generative AI and large language models, to demand prediction and traffic filtering. - Drive end-to-end optimization projects that tackle ambiguous problems at massive scale, developing scalable, efficient processes for model development, validation, and deployment that optimize traffic monetization while maintaining customer experience.
